title: The Festival Storybook Rescue
learning_focus: Identify character, setting, goal, and major events in a short narrative; use one clear noun–pronoun reference in a caption.
story_premise: During Bayang Haraya’s Storybook Village Festival, the opening chapter of the town storybook becomes incomplete. Farmer Lira asks the Pathfinder to inspect the illustrated clues, restore the event path, and rebuild the short chapter before the courtyard reading begins.
mission_objective: Identify the story’s character, setting, goal, and major events; reconstruct the event sequence; and complete the chapter with a suitable ending.

areas.title: Story Square
areas.story: Farmer Lira asks the Pathfinder to inspect the damaged opening page in Story Square. The learner identifies the character, setting, and goal, then repairs one caption so its pronoun clearly points to the children. The storybook stand repairs and Story Fragment 1 appears.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Farmer Lira
opening_dialogue.text: Pathfinder, the opening page is damaged. Inspect the picture and the surviving lines.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Farmer Lira
opening_dialogue.text: Find who is here, where the story begins, and what the children want to do. Then repair the missing caption.

learning_clues: A story opening introduces the character, setting, and goal.
A pronoun should clearly refer to a noun already named.

evidence_clues.title: Opening Illustration
evidence_clues.body: Look at the damaged opening picture. Who is in the scene, and where does the festival story begin?

evidence_clues.title: Surviving Lines
evidence_clues.body: Read the surviving sentence. What do the children want to do once the opening page is repaired?

questions.prompt: Who asks the Pathfinder to repair the opening page?
questions.first_wrong_hint: Look at the guide beside the damaged storybook.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Farmer Lira is the guide who asks the Pathfinder for help.
questions.correct_feedback: Farmer Lira is the guide who asks the Pathfinder for help.

options.text: In Story Square near the large acacia tree

questions.first_wrong_hint: Use the place shown in the opening picture and text.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The opening setting is Story Square near the large acacia tree.
questions.correct_feedback: The opening setting is Story Square near the large acacia tree.

questions.prompt: What do the children want to do?

options.text: Carry a friendship banner to the Chronicle Courtyard

questions.first_wrong_hint: Find the children’s goal in the surviving sentence.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The children’s goal is to carry the friendship banner to the Chronicle Courtyard.
questions.correct_feedback: The children’s goal is to carry the friendship banner to the Chronicle Courtyard.

areas.world_action: Place the correct opening caption and connect “They” to the children on the storybook stand.
areas.world_result: The opening page becomes readable, the storybook stand lights up, Story Fragment 1 appears, and the route to Banner Market Lane opens.
areas.story_source: Farmer Lira stands beside the damaged town storybook in Story Square. The opening picture shows children gathering near the large acacia tree. They plan to carry a friendship banner to the Chronicle Courtyard, but the opening caption is missing.

areas.title: Banner Market Lane
areas.story: Three illustrated event clues are scattered among the market stalls. The learner finds them, inspects their details, and arranges them in chronological order to restore the banner route. Story Fragment 2 appears when the sequence is correct.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Mina
opening_dialogue.text: Welcome to Banner Market Lane! The middle of the chapter fell off our stall banners.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Mina
opening_dialogue.text: Find the three event markers along the lane. Then place them in time order: first, next, and finally.

learning_clues: Events in a narrative follow a logical time order.
Sequence clues such as first, next, and finally show how events connect.

evidence_clues.title: First Banner Marker
evidence_clues.body: This near-stall banner shows what happened FIRST: the children gather under the acacia tree in Story Square before the market walk begins.

evidence_clues.title: Next Banner Marker
evidence_clues.body: This middle-stall painting shows what happened NEXT: after the children gather, Farmer Lira opens the damaged town storybook.

evidence_clues.title: Final Banner Marker
evidence_clues.body: This far-stall marker shows what happened FINALLY on the route: the Pathfinder repairs the missing opening caption so the banner path can continue.

questions.prompt: Which Banner Market Lane marker shows the FIRST event?

options.text: The children gather at the acacia tree.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Choose the marker that begins the story sequence.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The first Banner Market Lane marker is the children gathering at the acacia tree.
questions.correct_feedback: Yes — the children gathering at the acacia tree is first in the market-lane sequence.

questions.prompt: According to the stall markers, what happens NEXT after the children gather?

options.text: Farmer Lira opens the damaged storybook.
The final chapter is placed in the Chronicle.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Look at the middle-stall marker in the three-clue sequence.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Next comes Farmer Lira opening the damaged storybook.
questions.correct_feedback: Yes — Farmer Lira opens the damaged storybook next after the children gather.

questions.prompt: Which event belongs LAST on the Banner Market Lane sequence board?

options.text: The Pathfinder repairs the missing opening caption.
The children gather at the acacia tree.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Choose the far-stall marker that follows the storybook being opened.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Last in this market-lane sequence is the Pathfinder repairing the missing opening caption.
questions.correct_feedback: Yes — repairing the missing opening caption is last on the Banner Market Lane board.

areas.world_action: Place the three event markers in order on the banner-route board.
areas.world_result: The banners rise in the correct order, the market route opens, and Story Fragment 2 appears.
areas.story_source: Along Banner Market Lane, three stall markers must be ordered: FIRST the children gather at the acacia tree; NEXT Farmer Lira opens the damaged storybook; FINALLY the Pathfinder repairs the missing opening caption. The banner route activates only in that chronological order.

areas.title: Chronicle Courtyard
areas.story: At the courtyard Chronicle display, the learner uses the two recovered fragments and the restored event path to assemble a short beginning, middle, and ending. The learner chooses the ending that fits the goal and presents the completed chapter. Story Fragment 3 appears and the festival reading begins.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Farmer Lira
opening_dialogue.text: The opening and event path are restored. Now the Chronicle needs one complete chapter.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Farmer Lira
opening_dialogue.text: Use the evidence you found, choose the ending that fits, and present the story to the courtyard.

learning_clues: A coherent story has a beginning, middle, and ending.
The ending should resolve the character’s goal and fit the earlier events.

questions.prompt: Which sentence belongs in the beginning?

options.text: The children gather near the acacia tree in Story Square.
The Chronicle displays the finished chapter.

questions.first_wrong_hint: The beginning introduces the characters and setting.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The children gathering in Story Square belongs in the beginning.
questions.correct_feedback: The children gathering in Story Square belongs in the beginning.

questions.prompt: Which event belongs in the middle?

options.text: The Pathfinder restores the opening caption and event path.
The mission badge appears before the problem begins.
The courtyard reading happens before the children gather.
The storybook disappears after it is repaired.

questions.first_wrong_hint: The middle contains the actions taken to solve the problem.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Repairing the caption and event path belongs in the middle.
questions.correct_feedback: Repairing the caption and event path belongs in the middle.

questions.prompt: Which ending best fits the story?

options.text: The children bring the restored chapter to the courtyard and begin the festival reading together.
The children hide the chapter and cancel the festival.
A laboratory replaces the village festival.
The story ends before the missing page is repaired.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Choose the ending that completes the children’s goal and follows the restored event path.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The fitting ending shows the children reaching the courtyard and beginning the reading together.
questions.correct_feedback: The fitting ending shows the children reaching the courtyard and beginning the reading together.

areas.world_action: Assemble the beginning, middle, and ending, bind the three Story Fragments, and present the restored chapter at the Chronicle display.
areas.world_result: The Chronicle opens, the courtyard decorations light up, the restored chapter is read, Story Fragment 3 is collected, and the mission completes.
areas.story_source: Beginning: the children gather in Story Square and Farmer Lira reveals the damaged storybook. Middle: the Pathfinder repairs the opening caption and restores the event path through Banner Market Lane. The ending must show the children reaching the courtyard with the restored chapter and beginning the festival reading together.

competency_contract.primary_competency_summary: Identify character, setting, goal, and major events in a short narrative.
competency_contract.mastery_evidence: Learner reconstructs a coherent beginning, event sequence, and suitable ending using observed story evidence.
